lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: ask when locals eat, how long lunch lasts, coffee after meals, and afternoon closures
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: Ask a local why restaurants close at 3 p.m. and what counts as normal at a weekday lunch.
lessons.title: 昼食の時間と店の休憩を聞く
lessons.objective: Ask when people eat lunch, how long it lasts, whether coffee follows a meal, and why this restaurant closes between lunch and dinner.
lessons.focus: 昼食の時間 means lunchtime. 平日 means weekday. 営業時間 are opening hours, and 休憩時間 is the restaurant’s break. 食後 means after eating; 食後にコーヒーを頼みますか asks about coffee after the meal.
lessons.scene: A traveler arrives just as a small restaurant closes its kitchen after lunch.

cards.ja: この辺では何時ごろ昼食を食べますか。
cards.en: About what time do people eat lunch around here?

cards.ja: 昼食には普段どのくらい時間をかけますか。
cards.en: How long does lunch usually last?

cards.ja: なぜ午後三時に閉まるのですか。
cards.en: Why do you close at three in the afternoon?

cards.ja: 食後にコーヒーを頼むことは多いですか。
cards.en: Do people often order coffee after eating?

cards.ja: 営業時間を教えていただけますか。
cards.en: Could you tell me the opening hours?

cards.ja: 午後五時に戻れば開いていますか。
cards.en: Will you be open if I come back at five?

cards.ja: 明日の正午に席を予約できますか。
cards.en: Can I reserve a table for noon tomorrow?

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 火曜日の午後三時、旅行者が小さな食堂に入ります。
reader.en: At three on Tuesday afternoon, a traveler enters a small restaurant.

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: すみません。昼の厨房はもう閉まりました。
reader.en: I am sorry. The kitchen has closed for lunch.

reader.speaker: Traveler
reader.ja: なぜ午後三時に閉まるのですか。
reader.en: Why do you close at three in the afternoon?

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: この店は午後三時から五時まで休憩時間です。
reader.en: This restaurant takes a break from three until five.

reader.speaker: Traveler
reader.ja: この辺では何時ごろ昼食を食べますか。
reader.en: About what time do people eat lunch around here?

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: 平日は正午ごろ日替わり定食を頼むお客さんが多いです。
reader.en: On weekdays, many customers order the daily set meal around noon.

reader.speaker: Traveler
reader.ja: 昼食には普段どのくらい時間をかけますか。
reader.en: How long does lunch usually last?

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: この店では一時間ぐらいのお客さんが多いです。
reader.en: At this restaurant, many customers stay for about an hour.

reader.speaker: Traveler
reader.ja: 食後にコーヒーを頼んで、少し話してもいいですか。
reader.en: May we order coffee after eating and talk for a little while?

reader.speaker: Owner
reader.ja: はい。お会計の前でも大丈夫です。午後五時からまた営業します。
reader.en: Yes. That is fine before the check. We open again at five.

reader.speaker: Traveler
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。明日の正午に席を予約できますか。
reader.en: Thank you. Can I reserve a table for noon tomorrow?

speaking.role: Traveler asking about local lunch habits and restaurant hours
speaking.opening: すみません。昼の厨房はもう閉まりました。
speaking.goal: Ask why the restaurant closes at three, when locals eat, how long lunch lasts, whether coffee comes after the meal, and when it reopens.
speaking.closure: 明日の正午に席を予約できますか。

lessons.sourceEnglishTitle: Build a picnic at a deli
lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: order sliced foods by quantity, ask for packing and utensils, and ask where picnics are allowed
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: Put together a picnic for four at a deli counter and ask where you're allowed to eat it in the park.
lessons.title: 惣菜店でピクニックをそろえる
lessons.objective: Order ham and cheese by grams and slice thickness, ask for takeout packing and utensils for four, and ask where park picnics are allowed.
lessons.focus: 三百グラム and 二百グラム state quantities by weight. 薄切り means thin slices. 持ち帰り用に包んでください asks for takeout packing; ピクニックエリア names the designated picnic area.
lessons.scene: Ana buys sliced foods at a deli counter for four people before visiting the park.

cards.ja: ハムを三百グラムください。
cards.en: Three hundred grams of ham, please.

cards.ja: チーズを二百グラムください。
cards.en: Two hundred grams of cheese, please.

cards.ja: サンドイッチ用なので、薄切りでお願いします。
cards.en: Thin slices, please, because they are for sandwiches.

cards.ja: 持ち帰り用に包んでいただけますか。
cards.en: Could you pack it to go?

cards.ja: 四人分の食器と紙ナプキンをください。
cards.en: Utensils and napkins for four people, please.

cards.ja: 公園のどこでピクニックができますか。
cards.en: Where are picnics allowed in the park?

cards.ja: 入口の案内板で確認します。
cards.en: I will check the sign at the entrance.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: アナは四人分のピクニックのために公園の近くの惣菜店に来ます。
reader.en: Ana comes to a deli near the park to prepare a picnic for four.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: ハムを三百グラム、チーズを二百グラムください。
reader.en: Three hundred grams of ham and two hundred grams of cheese, please.

reader.speaker: Clerk
reader.ja: 厚切りと薄切り、どちらにしますか。
reader.en: Would you like thick or thin slices?

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: サンドイッチ用なので、薄切りでお願いします。
reader.en: Thin slices, please, because they are for sandwiches.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 持ち帰り用に包んでいただけますか。
reader.en: Could you pack it to go?

reader.speaker: Clerk
reader.ja: チーズは容器に入れて、ほかは袋に入れます。
reader.en: I will put the cheese in a container and the rest in a bag.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 四人分の食器と紙ナプキンをください。
reader.en: Utensils and napkins for four people, please.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 公園のどこでピクニックができますか。
reader.en: Where are picnics allowed in the park?

reader.speaker: Clerk
reader.ja: 案内板では、池のそばがピクニックエリアになっています。
reader.en: The sign says the picnic area is beside the pond.

reader.speaker: Clerk
reader.ja: 入口の案内板でも確認してください。
reader.en: Please also check the sign at the entrance.

reader.speaker: Ana
reader.ja: 分かりました。ありがとうございます。
reader.en: I understand. Thank you.

speaking.role: Customer building a picnic for four at a deli
speaking.opening: いらっしゃいませ。何グラムにしますか。
speaking.goal: Order 300 grams of ham and 200 grams of cheese in thin slices, request takeout packing and utensils, and ask where a park picnic is allowed.
speaking.closure: 入口の案内板で確認します。

lessons.sourceEnglishSkills: alert staff, ask someone to call emergency services, and say what was eaten
lessons.sourceEnglishScenario: Your friend starts reacting after a bite of street food; alert the vendor, ask for emergency help, and say what was eaten.
lessons.title: アレルギー反応を伝える
lessons.objective: Alert a food vendor to a friend’s allergic reaction, ask someone to call 119, identify peanuts in the sauce, and report what and when the friend ate and which medicine she used.
lessons.focus: アレルギー反応 means allergic reaction; ピーナッツアレルギー means peanut allergy. 喉が締め付けられる describes throat tightness. 救急車を呼んでください asks for an ambulance; in Japan the emergency number is 119.
lessons.scene: After a bite of street food, Elena develops an allergic reaction. Her friend speaks to the vendor, a bystander, and paramedics.

cards.ja: ピーナッツアレルギー
助けてください。友人にアレルギー反応が出ています。
cards.en: Help, please. My friend is having an allergic reaction.

cards.ja: 119番に電話して、救急車を呼んでください。
このソースにピーナッツは入っていますか。
彼女にはピーナッツアレルギーがあります。
五分前にこの料理を一口食べました。
cards.en: She took one bite of this food five minutes ago.

cards.ja: 薬はかばんの中にあります。
cards.en: Her medicine is in the bag.

cards.ja: 彼女はその薬をもう使いました。
cards.en: She has already used that medicine.

cards.ja: 喉が締め付けられると言っています。
cards.en: She says her throat feels tight.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 私は屋台にいます。友人のエレナが料理を一口食べたあと、せきをし始めました。
reader.en: I am at a food stand. After one bite, my friend Elena starts coughing.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 助けてください。友人にアレルギー反応が出ています。
reader.en: Help, please. My friend is having an allergic reaction.

reader.speaker: Elena
reader.ja: 喉が締め付けられる感じがします。
reader.en: My throat feels tight.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 彼女にはピーナッツアレルギーがあります。
reader.en: She has a peanut allergy.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 薬はかばんの中にあります。必要ですか。
reader.en: Your medicine is in the bag. Do you need it?

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: すみません。119番に電話して、救急車を呼んでください。
reader.en: Excuse me. Please call 119 for an ambulance.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: このソースにピーナッツは入っていますか。
reader.en: Does this sauce contain peanuts?

reader.speaker: Vendor
reader.ja: 原材料を確認します。はい、このソースにはピーナッツが入っています。
reader.en: I will check the ingredients. Yes, this sauce contains peanuts.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 救急車が着き、救急隊員がエレナの様子を聞きます。
reader.en: The ambulance arrives, and a paramedic asks about Elena.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 五分前にこの料理を一口食べました。
reader.en: She took one bite of this food five minutes ago.

reader.speaker: Friend
reader.ja: 彼女はかばんに入れていた薬をもう使いました。
reader.en: She has already used the medicine she carried in her bag.

speaking.role: Friend reporting a peanut-allergy reaction at a food stand
speaking.goal: State the allergic reaction and peanut allergy, ask for a 119 ambulance call, ask whether the sauce has peanuts, and report the bite, timing, throat tightness, and medicine already used.
speaking.closure: 五分前にこの料理を一口食べました。彼女は薬をもう使いました。
